morgan: quick heads-up — arch-scan found inconsistent SM reporting on 4 staging GPUs. affects kernel selection for long sequences (>1024) so perf falls back to a slow path. dumping traces and perf numbers below.

asha: which hosts? nvml vs cuda props?

morgan: hosts: staging-{a12,a13,b04,b05}. nvml gave sm_major=0 on b04 in one run, cudaDeviceGetAttribute returned 86. weird mismatch. suspect kernel driver vs nvml lib mismatch.

devon: oh nice catch. that would flip the tensorcore capability bit in our kernel selector. when SM reported 0 we chose older matmul kernel (no tf32/bf16) even though hw supports it.

morgan: exactly. quick repro snippet I ran:
```
# probe snippet
nvmlDeviceGetMinor(device, &minor);
nvmlDeviceGetMajor(&major);
if (major == 0) {
  // fallback to cuda api probe
  cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&v, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor, dev);
}
```
Sometimes nvml call times out and returns zeros.

liam: do we have a short-term mitigation? maybe prefer cudaDeviceQuery over nvml for selector or fallback delay-retry.

morgan: pushed a small patch to prefer cudaDeviceGetAttribute first, nvml only for nic info. infra-bot: deployed to staging.

infra-bot: arch-scan v0.9.3 deployed to staging at 2026-02-14T09:21Z :rocket:

asha: can we also make kernel selection resilient to transient probe failures? like a cached capability map per-node persisted for 24h, and a conservative fallback that still uses tensorcore if any indicator exists?

devon: I'd rather be explicit: if probe uncertain, run a micro-benchmark on first inference (cheap warmup) to pick kernel. micro-benchmarks: batch sizes [1,8], seq [64,512,2048], run 3 iters, pick fastest.

morgan: micro-benchmarks are good but add latency on cold-start. propose: async background probe on node startup that updates selector before traffic hits 90% capacity.

sophia: also saw a perf regression in canary yesterday for sequences around 1536 tokens — looks like we picked a 'packed-kv' kernel that loses on A100 for bf16 due to incompatible kernel tiling. attaching perf summary (short):

- host a12 (A100-sxm): batch=4 seq=1536 : packed-kv-bf16 = 12.3 ms, matmul-tc-bf16 = 8.9 ms (so selector picked wrong)
- host b04 (V100-like): batch=4 seq=1536 : packed-kv-bf16 = 13.1 ms, matmul-no-tc = 14.5 ms (packed wins)

Conclusion: selection must consider (sm_version, tensorcore_perf_ratio, seq_len) not just sm >= 80.

liam: agreed. propose we add a lightweight model: score = alpha*tc_speedup + beta*kv_locality - gamma*kernel_launch_overhead, where tc_speedup is measured from microbenchmarks. thresholds per-sequence-range.

asha: and add a regression alert: if new kernel choice increases p50 token latency by >10% on any canary host for seq bins [<=512, 513-1024, 1025-2048, >2048], fail rollout.

devon: adding to TODO: (1) prefer cuda probe, (2) async microbench at boot to populate per-node kernel stats, (3) selector model that is sequence-bin aware, (4) perf regression gate in rollout pipeline.

morgan: sounds good. I'll open a short PR with probe ordering + retry logic and add a follow-up RFC for selector model. tagging @asha @devon for review.

sophia: also recommend adding a small integration test for sm mismatch: mock nvml zeros and ensure selector falls back to cuda probe and microbench path. catches regression early.

morgan: thanks — will include test. :thumbsup:

liam: can someone add a dashboard panel showing node-level capability flags and last-probe-time? that'll help debugging.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-1427: "node capability: probe health + dashboard" assigned to infra oncall.

morgan: ok wrapping up. next steps: PR today for probe ordering + race fix, RFC next week for seq-aware selector, perf alerts added to canary pipeline.
